name: cookmarks
description: Work with your Cookmarks recipe library, meal plan and grocery list: search and read your saved recipes, plan meals, add ingredients to your grocery list, tick items off as you shop and import recipes from the web.

interface.longDescription:
Cookmarks is a recipe manager for home cooks. It saves recipes from any website into one library, then turns them into a meal plan and a grocery list.

Connect Cookmarks and ChatGPT can work with the recipes you've actually saved. Plan the week from your library, add a recipe's ingredients to your grocery list, check what's left to buy, or save a recipe you found while chatting. New to Cookmarks? ChatGPT can find recipes in the public Cookmarks collection and save the ones you like, or save a recipe it wrote for you as your own private recipe.

ChatGPT can search your library and the public Cookmarks collection, read recipes in full (with your own edits, notes and tags), and read your meal plan, cooking history and grocery list. With your permission it can save recipes to your library (including ones it wrote in the chat), add recipes to your meal plan, add items to your grocery list and import new recipes from web pages and supported social posts.

When you ask, it can also tick items off your grocery list, take items off it, and remove a recipe from your library. Those are the only things it can change or remove, and ChatGPT confirms with you before removing anything. It can't edit a recipe, and it can't see other people's private recipes or change your password, email or billing. Imports count toward the same allowance as importing on the website.

Sign in with your Cookmarks account to connect. Disconnect any time from Settings › Connected apps on cookmarks.app.
capabilities: Find and save recipes from the public Cookmarks collection
Save a recipe ChatGPT wrote in the chat as your own private recipe
Read a recipe with your edits, notes and tags
Read your meal plan and cooking history
Add a recipe to your meal plan
Add items or a recipe's ingredients to your grocery list
Add ingredients for every meal planned in a date range
Tick items off your grocery list, or take them off
Remove a recipe from your library when you ask
Import a recipe from a web page or social post
defaultPrompt: Find a quick vegetarian dinner on Cookmarks and save it.
Save this recipe to Cookmarks: (paste a link)
Plan 5 dinners for this week on Cookmarks and make the grocery list.

positive.description: Save a recipe ChatGPT wrote in the conversation to the library.
positive.prompt: Write me a simple weeknight lemon garlic chicken recipe, then save it to my Cookmarks library.
positive.expected_behavior: Writes the recipe in the chat, asks for confirmation, then calls create_recipe with its title, ingredient lines and steps (servings and times when it gave them). Reports it as saved with a cookmarks.app link. The recipe appears in the library at https://www.cookmarks.app/recipes as a private recipe labelled "Written with ChatGPT", not credited to any website.

positive.description: Add a saved recipe to the meal plan.
positive.prompt: Put my Cacio e Pepe on the Cookmarks meal plan for next Saturday.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds Cacio e Pepe with search_my_recipes, asks for confirmation, then calls plan_meal with next Saturday's date (a future date, so it is planned rather than logged as cooked). Confirms the meal is planned and links to the recipe on cookmarks.app. The entry appears at https://www.cookmarks.app/calendar.

positive.description: Add items to the grocery list, then tick one off.
positive.prompt: Add lemons and parmesan to my Cookmarks grocery list. Then tick off the lemons, I already have them.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls add_to_grocery_list with the two items, after asking for confirmation, and reports them as added with a link to https://www.cookmarks.app/shopping-list. Then calls check_grocery_items with the id of the lemons item (from the add result, or from get_grocery_list), after asking for confirmation. Reports the lemons as ticked off. On the list in Cookmarks, lemons shows as checked and parmesan as still to buy. It must not call remove_grocery_items: the user asked to tick the item off, not to delete it.

positive.description: Import a recipe from a web page into the library.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls import_recipe with the URL, after asking for confirmation. It usually returns status saved within 20 seconds; if it returns status importing with a job_id, calls get_import_status until it is saved. Reports the saved recipe, Maple Soy Glazed Salmon, with a cookmarks.app link. If the recipe is already in the library, says so.

positive.description: Find a new recipe in the public Cookmarks collection and save it to the library.
positive.prompt: Find me a quick vegetarian dinner on Cookmarks and save it to my library.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls search_public_recipes (for example with the query "quick vegetarian dinner") and lists a few matching public recipes. Recipes already in the reviewer library, such as Cacio e Pepe, are left out. Asks for confirmation, then calls save_recipe for the recipe the user picks (or the first one, if the user just confirms). Reports it as saved with a cookmarks.app link. The recipe then appears in the library at https://www.cookmarks.app/recipes. The exact results change as the public collection grows.

negative.description: A general recipe request that doesn't mention the user's Cookmarks library. ChatGPT should answer from its own knowledge. It may offer to save the recipe to Cookmarks, but must not call any Cookmarks write tool (create_recipe, save_recipe, plan_meal, add_to_grocery_list, import_recipe) unless the user says yes; a search of the public Cookmarks collection is acceptable but not expected.
negative.prompt: Give me a classic lasagna recipe.

negative.description: Cookmarks has no tool that edits a recipe. ChatGPT should say it can't change a saved recipe and point to the Cookmarks app. It must not call any write tool (in particular not remove_recipe or create_recipe to work around it); reading the recipe with get_recipe is acceptable.
negative.prompt: Change my Cacio e Pepe recipe in Cookmarks to serve 6.

negative.description: Cookmarks can't order or deliver groceries. ChatGPT should say so, may read the list with get_grocery_list, calls no write tools and never claims an order was placed.
negative.prompt: Order the items on my grocery list for delivery.

review.commerce_description: Cookmarks sells nothing through the plugin and takes no payment. Paid plans are bought on cookmarks.app, outside ChatGPT, and tool results contain no upgrade prompts.

publication.release_notes: Fifteen tools. New in 1.0.4: tick items off your grocery list or untick them (check_grocery_items), take items off the list (remove_grocery_items), and remove a recipe from your library (remove_recipe), each only when you ask. The two remove tools are marked destructive. A get-started setup skill looks at what a new account holds and offers one first step (save a first recipe, plan the week or start a grocery list), and the third starter prompt now works on an empty account. Unchanged: search and read your recipes, meal plan and grocery list; find and save public Cookmarks recipes; save a recipe written in the chat as your own private recipe; add recipes to your meal plan; add items and ingredients to your grocery list; import recipes from web pages and social posts, with a status check for longer imports; ask the Cookmarks team for help when an import fails. Served from https://www.cookmarks.app/api/mcp.
